You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Palantir Q2 Earnings Preview: Can Triple-Digit Commercial Growth Continue? AI Software Leader Faces Another “Beat and Raise” Test

TEXT:
1.Investment Highlights
Palantir ( PLTR .US) will report its fiscal Q2 2026 results after the U.S. market close on August 3, 2026. Wall Street consensus expects total revenue of approximately $1.81 billion (up ~81% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.34–$0.35 (more than doubling year-over-year). The company’s own guidance range is $1.797–$1.801 billion (midpoint implying ~79% growth). Oppenheimer and others are more optimistic, forecasting roughly 85% revenue growth and an upward revision of full-year guidance to above 75% (from the current >71%). With tech stocks remaining volatile, the market is closely watching whether U.S. commercial growth can sustain triple-digit rates, the durability of government business, and whether the company can once again deliver a “beat and raise.”
2. Four Key Focus Areas
Focus 1: Can U.S. Commercial Maintain Triple-Digit Growth? U.S. commercial remains the primary growth engine. The market expects Q2 U.S. commercial revenue growth of over 130–135% (some houses looking for 140%+), with full-year guidance already raised to at least 120%. In Q1 the segment reached $595 million (+133%). Oppenheimer notes that Palantir appeared largely immune to the deal push-outs seen at other software vendors and that demand stayed robust. Investors will focus on net retention rates (NRR), large-deal momentum, and actual monetization progress of the AIP platform.
Focus 2: Resilience of U.S. Government Business vs. International Drag U.S. government revenue is expected to grow in the low-80% range in Q2, driven by higher Department of Homeland Security spending and Middle East geopolitical tensions, with positive expansion across multiple U.S. military branches and combatant commands. International government business remains softer as several European allies continue seeking alternatives. Whether the overall government segment can continue serving as a stable anchor will be a key watchpoint.
Focus 3: Can Ontology and Agentic AI Defend Against Large-Model Competition? Market concerns persist that large-language-model providers deploying forward-deployed engineers could erode Palantir’s share. Oppenheimer believes these fears are overstated: Palantir’s Ontology is better suited for complex workflows, while LLMs tend to serve simpler use cases. Tools released at DevCon 6 in July—Orchestrator, Agent Engine, and Agent SDK—further strengthen the company’s edge. The earnings call will test commercial AI progress and differentiation.
Focus 4: Room for Full-Year Guidance Raise and Valuation Digestion Current full-year revenue guidance stands at approximately 71% growth ($7.65–$7.662 billion). A clear Q2 beat could lead the market to expect an upward revision above 75%. Meanwhile, PLTR has declined roughly 30% year-to-date and still carries a premium valuation; management commentary on the second half and Rule of 40 metrics will be critical for sentiment.
3. Risks and Opportunities
Upside Catalysts:
U.S. commercial growth significantly above consensus (>135%), confirming sustainability of triple-digit expansion.
Total revenue growth approaching or exceeding 85%, accompanied by a full-year guidance raise to >75%.
Continued strength in U.S. government business with manageable international drag, plus positive customer feedback on the AI platform.
Downside Risks:
U.S. commercial growth below expectations or signs of deceleration, raising questions about durability.
Results only in line with or slightly below guidance midpoint without a full-year raise, pressuring the high valuation.
Further weakness in international business or intensifying competition affecting commercial customer retention.
4. Trading Strategy Suggestions
Bull Case: If U.S. commercial and total revenue meaningfully beat consensus while management raises full-year guidance and provides a constructive outlook, it could reinforce confidence in Palantir as an AI software leader and support valuation recovery.
Bear Case: If core metrics merely meet or modestly miss expectations, commercial growth slows, or guidance remains cautious, profit-taking could follow—especially amid elevated tech-stock volatility.
Key Metrics to Watch:
Total revenue and year-over-year growth
U.S. commercial revenue growth and deal/contract trends
U.S. government revenue performance
Whether full-year revenue guidance is raised
Gross margin and Rule of 40 metrics
Trading Suggestion: If results beat expectations and guidance is constructive, consider opportunities on pullbacks. If data is in-line or guidance is soft, watch for short-term volatility and avoid chasing. Position size and stop-loss levels should be adjusted according to individual risk tolerance.
